title.en: The human digestive system: alimentary canal and glands

say.en: From the mouth to the anus the human alimentary canal is about eight to nine metres long, folded inside the abdomen, with glands pouring in juices along the way. In this lesson: Name the parts of the alimentary canal in order.
Describe the teeth and the wall of the gut.
Name the digestive glands and their secretions.

body.en: The *canal* runs: mouth (buccal cavity, teeth, tongue) → pharynx → oesophagus → stomach (cardiac, fundic, body, pyloric parts) → small intestine (duodenum, jejunum, ileum) → large intestine (caecum with appendix, colon, rectum) → anus. Its wall has four layers: serosa, muscularis, submucosa and mucosa (which forms villi). Adult humans have 32 diphyodont, thecodont, heterodont teeth (2123/2123). The glands are the salivary glands, gastric and intestinal glands, the liver (bile) and the pancreas (pancreatic juice and hormones).
